method:
Pictures first, then geometry.

1. Rendered the whole part with the shared render.py. Then rendered 16 tiles of 6.4 x 6.4 m at 0.5 m grid, with inserts and text: A1-D4, x 30.8-37.2 / 36.8-43.2 / 42.8-49.2 / 48.8-55.0 by y 20-26.4 / 14-20.4 / 8-14.4 / 4.8-8.4.
2. Many long WALL/COL lines are not walls: CENTER2 grid lines, HIDDEN overhead edges (for example x 38.995 and the canopy outline C4B8) and PHANTOM2 property lines. So I wrote a renderer variant (r2.py in my folder) that dashes non-continuous linetypes. With it I zoomed (0.05-0.2 m grid) on every wall group: den and porch, corridor/bath/small room, family room, glazed hall, stair, east service block, NE room, and the east boundary with its gates.
3. Confirmed every candidate from prims.pkl with a box query (q.py): wall line end points on both sides, JAMB inserts and jamb polylines, LEAF/SWING and door blocks (_1D3R90, XR_L44 Plan$0$D4, hjkhkk), layer-0 leaves and arcs, and window mullion/track patterns.
4. Completeness checks: clustered every DOOR, D-JAMB, WIN, WALL-GL and xref door/wall entity in the box (sweep.py) and listed every ARC on any layer (arcs.py). Each cluster or arc is either one of GE-01..18, furniture, or outside the box.
5. Used the elevations only to classify glazing. The right-hand drawing is an east view of this part: the ramp R-01 matches. In it AW1 (GE-10) and AD1 (hall glass) are full height, and D1 (GE-11) is a pivot door.
6. a and b sit on the middle of the WALL-layer thickness; 50 mm cladding on D-JAMB/layer 0 is excluded. The ends are at wall-end faces, or at the outer faces of jambs and frames.
7. Final check renders, with a marker and an a-b segment per opening: check1.png, check_zoomA-D.png and final_marks.png. No unmarked gap, swing, leaf, jamb pair or window group remained, apart from the items listed in uncertain and rejected.
